why: Cxcr4 is the mouse ortholog of human CXCR4 and encodes CXCR4 (CD184), a class A G-protein-coupled chemokine receptor that binds the chemokine CXCL12 (SDF-1). CXCR4 has been associated with hematopoietic cell trafficking, retention of stem cells in bone marrow, and immune-cell migration; it also serves as a co-receptor for certain strains of HIV.

CXCR4 is implicated in cancer metastasis and in WHIM syndrome, and CXCR4-directed agents are used for stem-cell mobilization and are under study in cancer. Homozygous Cxcr4-null mice show embryonic lethality with defects in hematopoiesis and vascular and neural development.
applications: Humanized CXCR4 models, in which the human receptor replaces the mouse counterpart, have been used to evaluate CXCR4-directed agents in defined experimental settings.
Conditional Cxcr4 models have been used to study cell trafficking and hematopoiesis.

why: Mstn is the mouse ortholog of human MSTN and encodes myostatin (GDF8), a secreted TGF-β-superfamily factor produced mainly by skeletal muscle. Myostatin has been associated with negative regulation of muscle mass.

Loss of myostatin function increases muscle mass in several species, and myostatin-pathway-directed agents are under study for muscle-wasting and metabolic conditions. Mstn-deficient mice show marked increases in skeletal muscle mass.
applications: Humanized MSTN models, in which the human protein replaces the mouse counterpart, have been used to evaluate myostatin-directed agents in defined experimental settings.
